Statute
STAT-ūt
n. (rendering Hebrew chōq and chuqqâh)
From Latin statutum, that which is set up or established, from statuere, to set — the same root as stand and statue. The Hebrew is even more concrete: chōq comes from chāqaq, to cut, to engrave, to inscribe — a statute is something cut in, carved on stone or tablet, and therefore fixed and not to be revised by the reader. The English and the Hebrew agree in making permanence the point.

Biblical Definition

The statutes are the engraved, fixed appointments of God for His people, and the Old Testament ordinarily lists them alongside commandments and judgments as one of the branches of the law. Their purpose is stated as mercy rather than mere authority: “And the LORD commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive” (Deu 6:24) — for our good always, which is the answer to every suspicion that God's law is arbitrary restriction. Their character is likewise commended: “The statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes” (Psa 19:8). The believer's proper relation to them is neither grudging compliance nor indifference but delight, expressed in one of the most striking lines of the long psalm: “Thy statutes have been my songs in the house of my pilgrimage” (Psa 119:54) — the law set to music by a man on the road. But Scripture is honest that the statutes cannot of themselves produce obedience in a fallen heart, which is why the new covenant promise is not a better code but a changed man: “And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them” (Eze 36:27). The law remains what it was; the difference lies in the Spirit given, and in a heart of flesh replacing the heart of stone.

Webster 1828 Definition

An engraved and established appointment of God, listed with the commandments and judgments as a branch of His law; given for the good of His people, right and heart-rejoicing, sung by the pilgrim, and kept only where the Spirit causes a man to walk in them.

expand to see more

STATUTE, n. 1. An act of the legislature of a state that extends its binding force to all the citizens or subjects of that state; a positive law.

2. A special law for the government of a corporation or society; the statutes of a university.

3. In Scripture, an ordinance or appointment of God; the Hebrew word signifying that which is engraven or cut in, and thus fixed and permanent. Exod. 12; Levit. 3.

4. Statutes, judgments and commandments; the usual threefold division of the Mosaic law in the books of Moses and in the Psalms.

5. A statute for ever; an ordinance appointed to continue throughout the generations of Israel, as the passover and the day of atonement. Levit. 16.

Key Scripture

Deuteronomy 6:24 — "And the LORD commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive, as it is at this day."

Psalm 19:8 — "The statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes."

Psalm 119:54 — "Thy statutes have been my songs in the house of my pilgrimage."

Ezekiel 36:27 — "And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them."

Modern Corruption

God's statutes are treated as an obsolete legal code, so that the whole law is either discarded as bondage or re-imposed indiscriminately — both failing to distinguish the moral law that abides from the ceremonial and civil appointments fulfilled in Christ.

expand to see more

Antinomianism reasons that because the believer is not under law but under grace, the statutes have no further claim on him. Paul asks and answers the question directly: do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law. The law cannot justify a sinner — that was never its office — but it remains the revelation of God's character and the rule of gratitude for those He has saved. The Reformed tradition speaks of its three uses: it restrains evil in society, it convicts the sinner and drives him to Christ, and it guides the believer in the way of holiness. Where the third use is lost, sanctification loses its shape, and Christians are left sincere and directionless.

The opposite error takes the whole Mosaic corpus as binding without distinction, and so reimposes dietary laws, festival calendars, and the judicial penalties of Israel's civil polity on the Christian church. Scripture itself makes the distinctions. The ceremonial statutes were shadows of things to come, the body being Christ's; the Lord declared all meats clean; the civil statutes governed a particular nation in a particular land under a covenant that has expired with that polity, though their general equity remains instructive. The moral law, summarised in the ten commandments and by Christ in the two great commandments, binds all men always because it reflects God's unchanging nature. Eze 36:27 remains the hope in every case: the promise is not a lighter law but a Spirit who causes His people to walk in it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew chōq and its feminine chuqqâh come from chāqaq, to cut or engrave, and so name a fixed, inscribed decree. They stand alongside mitsvâh (commandment), mishpāt (judgment), and tōrâh (law, instruction).

expand to see more

Hebrew chōq (H2706) — a statute, a decree, an appointed portion; from chāqaq (H2710), to cut in, to engrave, to inscribe.

Hebrew chuqqâh (H2708) — ordinance, statute; the feminine form, used of the passover and the day of atonement as a statute for ever.

Hebrew mishpāt (H4941) — judgment, ordinance, legal decision; the case-law branch, usually paired with statutes.

Hebrew mitsvâh (H4687) — commandment, precept; the direct charge, as in the ten commandments.

Hebrew tōrâh (H8451) — law, instruction, direction; from yārâh, to point or teach — the whole body of divine teaching within which the statutes stand.

Usage

"Of the law's purpose and character: to do all these statutes…for our good always (Deu 6:24); the statutes of the LORD are right (Psa 19:8)."

"Of the believer's delight: thy statutes have been my songs in the house of my pilgrimage (Psa 119:54); I will delight myself in thy statutes (Psa 119:16)."

"Of the new covenant remedy: I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes (Eze 36:27)."
